wohnen.et: From Middle High German wonen, from Old High German wonēn, from Proto-West Germanic *wunēn, from Proto-Germanic *wunāną, from Proto-Indo-European *wenh₁- (“to wish, love”). Cognate with Bavarian wohna, Alemannic German wohne, Hunsrik wohne.

s: possibly, probably; as I was told (modal particle expressing an assumption, often like English must + infinitive, or (US) guess + clause)
He must have left already. / I guess he has left already.
Seine Frau ist wohl irgendeine bekannte Ärztin.
[I heard that] his wife is some well-known doctor.
of course, indeed (modal particle adding stress to the statement to contradict a preceding one, often like English do + infinitive)
Du warst ja noch nie in Frankreich. − Ich war wohl schon in Frankreich!
"Since you've never been to France..." − "Of course I've been to France!"
Ich kann's dir nicht sagen, weil ich's nicht weiß. − Du weißt es ja wohl!
"I can't tell you because I don't know." − "But you do know!"
actually, somehow, quite (modal particle making the statement weaker or expressing a concession)
Was habt ihr denn alle mit der Suppe? Ich find die wohl nicht schlecht.
"Why are you all complaining about the soup? I don't find it all that bad, actually."
Ihr habt wohl gesprochen, mein Herr!
yes; surely; really; on the contrary
That's not correct. — Yes, it is!
Kommst du heute Abend nicht? — Wohl!
Aren't you coming tonight?? — Yes, I am!
wohl.et: From Middle High German wol, wole, from Old High German wola (“well”), from Proto-Germanic *wela, from Proto-Indo-European *welh₁-. Compare Dutch wel, English well, Danish vel, Swedish väl.

s: domicile; dwelling; lodging; abode; accommodation (any place someone lives in for a span of time longer than a holiday)
flat; apartment (such a place when it occupies only part of a building)
Wohnung.et: From Middle High German wonunge, from Old High German wonunga, from Proto-West Germanic *wunungu, equivalent to wohnen + -ung. Related to Dutch woning (“house, residence”), English woning (“dwelling-place”). More at woning.

Wohl.et: From Middle High German wole, from Old High German wolo, welo (“weal, wealth, speed, prosperity”). More at weal.

s: how (not the general meaning of "in which way", but meaning "from which source" or "from where" exactly)
Ficken stand in unserem Wohnzimmer wie der runde Esstisch, das Sofa und das Bücherregal.

Wohnwagen.et: From wohnen (“to live, dwell, stay”) + Wagen (“vehicle, wagon, car”).

Wohlstand.et: wohl + Stand, 18th c. Compare Dutch welstand.

wohl oder übel.et: Literally, “well or badly”, that is "whether it be good or bad for us", or "whether we like it or not".

Er ist ein bisschen angeschickert. — Sternhagelvoll, wohl eher.

Wohnstallhaus.et: From wohnen (“live, dwell”) + Stall (“stable, barn”) + Haus (“house”).

Wohltat.et: From Middle High German woltāt, from Old High German wolatāt, woletāt, from Proto-Germanic *weladēdiz. By surface analysis, Wohl + Tat.

residential area, residential district, residential neighborhood

wohlschmeckend.et: wohl (“well”) + schmeckend (“tasting”). Compare Danish velsmagende, Swedish välsmakande.

Wohnanschrift.et: From wohnen (“to live, reside, dwell”) + Anschrift (“address”).

wohlgestaltet.et: wohl + gestaltet, in place of the older and original wohlgestalt.

wohlgestalt.et: Inherited from Middle High German wohlgestalt. By surface analysis, wohl + gestellt or wohl + Gestalt.

s: multifamily residential, multidwelling unit (classification of housing where multiple separate housing units for residential inhabitants are contained within one building or several buildings within one complex)

When Anneliese works in the garden, she wisely does not wear jewelry and only her oldest clothes.
wohlweislich.et: wohl (“well”) + weislich (“wisely”), a now archaic derivation from weise. Compare wohl wissend ("knowing full well").

The social market economy was the foundation for the German prosperous society.
